work.author: Jingjing
work.edition: Translated by Alexander Wylie (1855), as reprinted in Paul Carus (ed.), The Nestorian Monument: An Ancient Record of Christianity in China (Chicago: Open Court, 1909), 11–20; English Wikisource transcription
work.title: Tablet Eulogizing the Propagation of the Illustrious Religion in China (Xi'an Stele)

work.edition: Chinese Wikisource, «景教三威蒙度讚», revision 485789 (2016-07-20); diplomatic text of Pelliot chinois 3847 (Dunhuang; Bibliothèque nationale de France). A Chinese adaptation of the Gloria in excelsis; listed as 三威讚經 in the Zunjing.
work.title: 景教三威蒙度讚 (Hymn to the Holy Trinity)

work.edition: Chinese Wikisource, «大秦景教流行中國碑頌», revision 5621233 (2026-05-24); the Syriac (Estrangela) inscriptions of the Xi'an stele of 781: the byline of Adam, the dating under Patriarch Ḥnanishoʿ, the year 1092 of the Greeks, Yazdbozid's dedication and the clergy's names, numbered as the Chinese units they stand beside (wikisource-lzh/xian-stele). ⁎ marks illegible letters.
work.title: ܟܬܒܐ ܕܠܘܚܐ (Xi'an Stele, Syriac inscriptions)

work.author: 景淨
work.edition: Chinese Wikisource, «大秦景教流行中國碑頌», revision 5621233 (2026-05-24); diplomatic transcription of the stele erected in 781 at Chang'an (now in the Xi'an Beilin Museum), with the names on its sides; the Syriac is the separate work xian-stele-syriac. The later inscriptions of 1859 and 1917 are left out.
work.title: 大秦景教流行中國碑頌并序 (Xi'an Stele)

work.edition: Chinese Wikisource, «大秦景教宣元至本經», revision 517908 (2016-09-26); the text of the Luoyang sutra pillar (經幢, dated 元和九年十二月 = 814/815, excavated 2006) and the pillar's dedication (幢記); …… and □ mark damaged text. The page's other witnesses are not included: the Dunhuang manuscript (Li Shengduo's 宣元本經) and Kojima manuscript B, a modern forgery (Lin Wushu). Listed in the Zunjing among the books Jingjing translated.
work.title: 大秦景教宣元至本經 (Book of the Origin of Origins), Luoyang pillar

work.edition: Chinese Wikisource, «序聽迷詩所經», revision 447399 (2015-11-03); text of the manuscript formerly in Tomioka Kenzō's collection (Kyōu Shooku 羽459); the end is lost. Traditionally dated to Aluoben's mission, c. 635–638, as one of the earliest Jingjiao texts; its authenticity and date are debated (the manuscript surfaced through the antiquities trade, like 一神論, and some scholars doubt it or date it later).
work.title: 序聽迷詩所經 (Jesus-Messiah Sutra)

work.edition: Chinese Wikisource, «志玄安樂經», revision 2009893 (2020-12-26); reading text of the manuscript formerly in Li Shengduo's collection, published in Kyōu Shooku's Tonkō hikyū (Osaka); □ marks the manuscript's gaps. Its beginning is lost. Listed in the Zunjing among the books Jingjing translated.
work.title: 志玄安樂經 (Book of Profound and Mysterious Peace and Joy)
